A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Layer-wise Feedback Propagation (LFP) work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including proofs, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments, activation comparisons, pruning analyses, and SNN training results, including supplementary experiments in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds optimizer timing comparisons, activation-noise experiments, larger SNN evaluations, regression, and transformer fine-tuning results.

M1.justification: The basic LFP update remains unchanged, but v3 adds substantive adaptations: training-time activation noise for Heaviside DNNs (Section 3.6), regression rewards (Appendix A.8), and LayerNorm/attention propagation for transformers (Appendix A.9). The regression demonstration retains the zero reference point; its possible correction is discussed rather than implemented.

E1.justification: v3 adds California Housing regression and bean-disease image classification (Appendices A.8–A.9), extending the classification-focused v2 into tabular regression and an agricultural image domain. The original datasets remain; additional architectures on MNIST and CIFAR10 primarily expand experimental settings.

E2.justification: Beyond v2's ordinary and surrogate-enabled gradient comparisons, v3 evaluates feedback alignment, PSO, and dlADMM in Figure 5, with dlADMM restricted to the MLP. Figure 11 adds R-STDP, although its original architecture differs from the modified architecture used for LFP and gradient-based training.

E3.justification: v3 introduces 50-epoch MNIST timing comparisons, noise/no-noise Heaviside experiments lasting 300/400 epochs, and larger CIFAR10 SNN evaluations with 25 time steps (Sections 3.4, 3.6, 4.2). New regression and ViT protocols use 100 epochs, with MSE evaluation and frozen ViT embeddings respectively. These are added protocols rather than replacements for Table 3's settings.

E4.justification: Section 3.6 adds controlled activation-noise experiments and tracks inactive neurons to investigate the Heaviside failure observed in v2. Appendix A.4 adds a SiLU minimization/maximization case study comparing update trajectories. Section 4.2 also reports a surrogate-invariance sanity check for LFP; the original supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Matched experiments retain their run counts, seed-setting procedure, and uncertainty reporting. v3 extends the existing three-seed mean/standard-deviation convention to the new CIFAR10 SNN and ViT results. Five-draw toy evaluations are unchanged; no increased replication or new statistical estimation procedure is established.

E6.justification: v3 adds runtime/accuracy findings, improved learning under activation noise, and CIFAR10 SNN curves favoring LFP over surrogate gradients. It also reports California Housing test MSE of 0.33 and slower, poorer ViT convergence than gradient descent. These are newly reported experiments; Table 3 and the matched original result plots retain their values.

T1.justification: The ReLU theorem and its inductive proof are retained, but v3 corrects their overbroad generalization to any piecewise-linear activation, including Heaviside. Section 3.3 and Appendix A.2 instead require phi(z) = z phi'(z), explicitly excluding Heaviside, and clarify that practical LFP-epsilon is outside the stated LFP-0 equivalence.

C1.justification: The four numbered contributions and two principal applications remain. v3 modestly broadens the contribution framing to include preliminary regression and transformer demonstrations (Section 1.2), and strengthens the SNN performance claim from similar accuracy to similar or sometimes better accuracy than surrogate-gradient training (Section 5.1).

C2.justification: v3 adds a Hebbian interpretation of the update, develops the dead-neuron/pretraining explanation, and explicitly qualifies LFP as biologically implausible because of symmetric feedback and backward propagation. It also discusses the noise intervention's long training budget, regression reference-point concerns, and transformer convergence limitations.

D1.justification: Appendices A.7–A.9 substantially expand reproducibility information with comparator hyperparameters and implementation links, larger SNN configurations, regression architecture and reward settings, and the ViT checkpoint, optimizer, and frozen embeddings. These accompany newly added experiments. The activation-noise intervention's distribution and magnitude are not specified.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against feedback alignment, target propagation, Hebbian learning, equilibrium propagation, DECOLLE, and R-STDP. It distinguishes LFP's biological properties and requirements more explicitly. Related work on concept discovery, sparse autoencoders, and mechanistic interpretation also expands beyond v2's coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract and approach narrative are edited and reordered, layer-index notation is standardized, and the existing complexity discussion becomes a separate subsection. Appendix material is regrouped and duplicated SNN setup prose is removed. Beyond the scientific additions, the overall motivation–method–applications–discussion structure remains.

P2.justification: v3 adds substantial visual evidence in Figures 5–6, 10–11, and A.3–A.5, revises Figure 1, and regroups several retained appendix plots. Original result graphics are largely reused rather than replaced. Figure 11 introduces an inconsistency: its caption says training accuracy while its axis says test accuracy.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important gaps in v2 by empirically checking computational overhead, testing and partly mitigating the Heaviside dead-neuron failure, and correcting the theoretical equivalence's overbroad scope. The regression and ViT experiments also clarify applicability, including unfavorable transformer results. Incomplete noise specifications and architecture/labeling problems in the R-STDP comparison limit some additions, but the stronger validation and clearer qualifications constitute a substantial overall improvement.
